about.title: Hidden Hills Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Hidden Hills is a small, gated equestrian community in Los Angeles County, and most premises liability situations here trace back to private residences, equestrian facilities, common areas, or shared roadways like Jed Smith Road, El Dorado Meadow Road, and Lewis And Clark Road. Because the city is largely residential and privately governed, a fall can happen on a walkway, a stable, a private drive, or inside a home during a gathering. California law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to correct or warn about it. That's why early documentation matters so much: photos of the condition, witness names, and any available surveillance footage can make the difference in a claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you with an independent attorney who evaluates these details and works on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network can help gather the evidence that speaks to that timeline.

items.title: We Know Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from private residences or facilities is often overwritten within days. Acting quickly to preserve that footage can matter more than almost anything else in your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you bear some responsibility for the fall — it simply adjusts the final recovery rather than blocking it.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Hidden Hills?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for a premises liability claim. If a government entity owns or maintains the property involved, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. An attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the fall happened on private property in a gated community?
items.answer: Hidden Hills is largely made up of private residences and gated common areas, and premises liability law still applies whether the property is a private home, an equestrian facility, or a shared roadway. The key question remains whether the owner or manager knew or should have known about the hazardous condition. An independent attorney can help sort out who is responsible in these private-property situations.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free. Attorneys in our network typically work on a contingency fee basis, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
